home.title: Questions about rtylr
home.intro: The six things buyers ask first. Answers are on the page, not hidden behind markup.

items.question: What is rtylr?
items.answer: rtylr is the business suite for small and mid-sized companies. It brings sales, inventory, people, customers, finance and operations together on one shared data model, so a team stops stitching a register, a spreadsheet, an accounting tool and a task tracker together. Built for restaurants, retail and services businesses running 2 to 200 staff.

items.question: How much does rtylr cost?
items.answer: rtylr has not published its prices yet. The Free plan is genuinely free, needs no card, and covers 10 team members at one location with the core rtylr suite, so you can run a location on it today. Pro and Scale are quoted: tell us your team size and how many locations you run. See rtylr.com/pricing for what each plan includes.

items.question: Can I start with one workflow?
items.answer: Yes. You can start with the workflow that matters most to your business, while everything stays in one rtylr workspace and on one shared data model. The suite grows with you, without separate logins or exports.

items.question: Does rtylr replace my point-of-sale system?
items.answer: Yes. rtylr POS is a full-service register for restaurants and retail. It handles tickets, splits, tips, modifiers, inventory counts, offline mode and receipt printing on certified hardware. It runs on iPad, Android tablet and desktop, and it syncs in real time with the rest of the platform, so a sale moves stock without an export.

items.question: Is my data mine?
items.answer: Yes. Every rtylr account exports clean CSVs of customers, orders, staff, invoices and inventory at any time from the settings page, with no support ticket. Data lives in the EU or US region, your choice. See rtylr.com/trust for compliance detail and rtylr.com/legal/security for the security architecture.

items.question: What does rtylr replace?
items.answer: For most businesses that adopt it: a register, an inventory sheet, a scheduling tool, a payroll export, a customer list and an accounting package. The claim rtylr makes is not that each of those is worse on its own. It is that running them separately means the same number is entered more than once, and the versions disagree.

items.question: How much does rtylr cost?
items.answer: rtylr has not published its prices yet. The Free plan is genuinely free and needs no card, so you can run a location on it today. For Pro or Scale, contact us and we will talk through your team size and locations. We would rather quote you honestly than put a number here we might change.

items.question: Can I switch plans at any time?
items.answer: Yes. Upgrade and the new features unlock instantly. Downgrade and the change applies at the end of the current period. Your data, team, and settings stay put.

items.question: Is there a free trial for Pro?
items.answer: Every new workspace starts with a 14-day Pro trial, and it needs no card. At day 14 it reverts to the Free plan automatically unless you tell us otherwise.

items.question: What happens when I hit 10 seats on Free?
items.answer: You're prompted to move to Pro before adding seat 11. Nothing breaks. Your data, reports, and configurations all carry over.

items.question: When does Scale apply?
items.answer: Scale is built for teams past 30 active seats. It removes the seat and location limits and adds SSO, audit logs, a dedicated success manager and an SLA.

items.question: Any contract or lock-in?
items.answer: None. You can cancel at any time, and your data is exportable while the account is open.

items.question: Does rtylr POS work offline?
items.answer: Yes. rtylr POS keeps a full local copy of the menu, modifiers and active orders. When the internet drops, the register keeps taking orders, printing tickets and processing cash. Card transactions queue and settle automatically once the connection returns, so a Saturday night outage does not stop the floor.

items.question: What hardware works with rtylr POS?
items.answer: rtylr POS runs on iPad, Android tablet and Windows or macOS desktop. It pairs with Epson and Star receipt printers, standard barcode scanners, Zebra and Symbol scanners for retail, and Stripe Terminal, Clover and Square card readers. See rtylr.com/hardware for the tested list.

items.question: Can rtylr POS handle multi-location restaurants?
items.answer: Yes, on the Pro plan and above. Each location gets its own menu, pricing, staff and reporting, and the owner gets one consolidated dashboard across every site. A menu change can be pushed to all locations at once or tuned per location.

items.question: What does rtylr POS replace?
items.answer: The register, and the work that usually sits behind it: the stock count someone redoes by hand, the tips spreadsheet that feeds payroll, and the end-of-day export into accounting. Because the POS writes to the same database as ERP, HR and Finance, a sale updates stock and revenue as it happens rather than overnight.

items.question: What does rtylr ERP manage?
items.answer: rtylr ERP covers inventory, suppliers, purchase orders, stock transfers between locations, low-stock alerts and cost tracking. It reads item sales from the POS as they happen, so on-hand stock stays accurate without a nightly sync.

items.question: Does rtylr ERP support multi-warehouse inventory?
items.answer: Yes. Every item can be stocked at multiple locations with per-location counts, reorder thresholds and transfer tracking. A purchase order can be split across warehouses, and staff see only their assigned location by default.

items.question: What does rtylr ERP replace?
items.answer: The stock spreadsheet, and the CSV that was supposed to keep it in step with sales. A sale in the POS depletes the recipe components in ERP at the moment it happens, so "how many units of one component remain across three locations" is a question you can answer without opening a second tool.

items.question: What does rtylr CRM track?
items.answer: rtylr CRM tracks customers, visits, purchases, loyalty points and campaign touchpoints. For restaurants and retail it captures who ordered what straight from the POS, with no import. For services businesses you can log contacts, notes and deal stages by hand.

items.question: Does rtylr CRM have email marketing?
items.answer: Yes. Segment customers by purchase history, loyalty tier or custom tags, then send branded email campaigns. Open and click tracking are built in. SMS campaigns are available on the Pro plan through the Twilio integration.

items.question: What does rtylr CRM replace?
items.answer: The loyalty app, the mailing list, and the export that connects them to what people actually bought. Because CRM shares a database with the POS, a segment like "spent above average, has not visited in 60 days" stays current on its own instead of being rebuilt from a CSV each month.

items.question: What does rtylr HR do?
items.answer: rtylr HR handles employee records, scheduling, shift swaps, time-off requests, payroll runs and compliance documents. It supports restaurant-specific workflows including tip pooling, minor work-hour limits and split shifts, alongside general retail and services HR.

items.question: Does rtylr HR run payroll for the US?
items.answer: rtylr HR calculates gross-to-net pay, taxes and withholdings, and exports pay files compatible with Gusto, ADP and Rippling for filing. Direct filing through rtylr is on the roadmap. For now rtylr does the calculation and a third-party provider does the IRS filing.

items.question: Can staff see their schedule on their phone?
items.answer: Yes. Every staff member gets a mobile view of their schedule, time-off balance and shift swap requests. They can request a swap and submit time off from their phone without an admin account.

items.question: What does rtylr HR replace?
items.answer: The scheduling tool, the time-off inbox, and the double entry that happens when a new hire is created in HR, again in payroll, again in the CRM and again in access control. In rtylr the person is created once and the schedule, the pay run and the POS login all read the same record.

items.question: What does rtylr Finance handle?
items.answer: rtylr Finance handles invoicing, expenses, bill payments, bank reconciliation, and profit and loss, balance sheet and cash flow reports. Revenue from the POS, Stripe and other integrations arrives automatically. Expenses can come from a bank feed or be entered by hand.

items.question: Can rtylr Finance replace QuickBooks?
items.answer: For many small businesses, yes: invoicing, expenses, reconciliation, P&L and tax reports are all covered. A business with complex audit requirements or multi-entity consolidation may still want a dedicated ledger, and rtylr Finance exports to QuickBooks and Xero for exactly that case. That limit is worth knowing before you switch.

items.question: Does rtylr Finance support multiple currencies?
items.answer: Yes. Invoice in any currency, and rtylr converts using the exchange rate at invoice time. P&L reports can be read in any reporting currency, with FX lines shown explicitly rather than folded into the totals.

items.question: What does rtylr Finance replace?
items.answer: The month-end export. Revenue, refunds, tips, purchase orders and payroll already live in the same database as the ledger, so the close does not begin with reconciling four systems against each other. That is the difference the page is really claiming, and it is the one a standalone accounting package cannot make.

items.question: What is rtylr Flow?
items.answer: Flow is rtylr's project and task management app. It has kanban boards, lists, timeline views, cycles, milestones, custom fields and automations. What makes it different from a standalone tracker is that it reads the rest of your business: who is on shift from HR, which customer a project belongs to from CRM, and which work is billable from Finance.

items.question: What can Flow do that a standalone task tracker cannot?
items.answer: Assign a task to a staff member who already exists in HR, attach it to a customer who already exists in CRM, and push billable hours onto an invoice in Finance, without copying anything between tools. The tasks, boards, comments and automations you would expect are all there; the connection to real business records is the part a separate tracker cannot have.

items.question: Does Flow have a free tier?
items.answer: Yes. Flow is part of the rtylr suite, covering 10 team members at one location with unlimited projects, tasks, comments and attachments. Pro and Scale raise the team and location limits and add the controls a larger team needs. rtylr does not publish prices yet, so Pro and Scale are quoted.

items.question: What should I prepare for the demo?
items.answer: Nothing is required. If you would rather see your own data than a sample, bring a menu or a SKU list, a recent invoice, and a rough idea of how many people and how many locations you run. Those are enough to show the register, stock, payroll and the books working against something you recognise.

items.question: Is the demo a sales call?
items.answer: It is a 30 minute product walkthrough, run by someone who built rtylr. You do not need one in order to start: the Free plan covers 10 team members at one location and needs no card, so you can sign up and look around on your own first. The walkthrough is for the questions a signup page cannot answer.

items.question: Can the demo cover self hosting?
items.answer: Yes. rtylr can be self hosted, and the setup is documented publicly at docs.rtylr.com/self-hosting. Say so when you book, under Explore a Rtylr Use Case, and the walkthrough can go that way instead. The documentation is open, so you can also read it first and arrive with specific questions about your own infrastructure.

claims.title: One data model, no sync seams

claims.title: An OpenAPI document, published
claims.body: This site publishes a spec for its own endpoints as OpenAPI 3.1. It covers the marketing site, not the product API, and it is linked here so nobody has to guess which.

overview.p1: This Privacy Policy describes how Voxire (“we”) collects, uses, shares, and protects personal data in connection with the rtylr platform. We act as a data controller for personal data about our customers and website visitors, and as a data processor for Customer Data that our customers process in rtylr on behalf of their own end-users.
overview.p2: If you are an end-user of a business that uses rtylr (for example, a diner whose email is captured in a restaurant’s CRM), the rtylr customer is the controller of your data. Please contact that business first to exercise your rights; we will help them do so.

subsections.heading: Account and billing data
subsections.body: When you create a workspace we collect name, email, business name, role, country, and a password hash. When you subscribe, our payment processor (Paddle) collects billing address, tax identifiers, and card tokens. We do not store raw card numbers on our servers.

subsections.heading: Customer Data
subsections.body: Depending on the applications your business uses, Customer Data can include customer contact and loyalty records, orders, employee and payroll records, recruitment applications and CVs, invoices, schedules, and tasks. The business determines why this data is collected and supplies its own notices and lawful basis. A privacy-policy acknowledgement is not consent to unrelated marketing.

subsections.heading: Usage and device data
subsections.body: We log IP address, browser/device type, referring URL, pages accessed, and timestamps. We use this to operate, secure, and improve rtylr, and to generate aggregate analytics.

subsections.heading: Cookies and similar technologies
subsections.body: See the <cookiesAnchor>Cookies</cookiesAnchor> section below for details.

list1: provide, secure, and maintain the Service;
process billing and send transactional emails;
respond to support requests and improve product quality;
detect and prevent fraud, abuse, and security incidents;

comply with legal obligations and enforce our Terms.

list1: Contract, to provide the Service and manage billing.
Legitimate interests, to secure the Service, detect abuse, and improve features. We balance these interests against your rights.
Consent, for non-essential cookies and certain marketing communications. You can withdraw consent at any time.
Legal obligation, when we are required to retain or disclose data by law.

sharing.p1: We use service providers and other recipients to operate rtylr. Their legal role depends on the service: a payment merchant may act as an independent controller rather than a subprocessor. The providers named in this notice include:
list1: Cloudflare, CDN, DNS, DDoS protection.
Paddle, payment processing and merchant of record.
Firebase / Google Cloud, authentication infrastructure.
Resend / Postmark, transactional email delivery.
PostHog / Axiom, product analytics and error tracking (when enabled).

list1: Account data is retained for the life of the account plus 30 days for recovery, then deleted within 60 days.

object to or restrict processing;
